question:
A DNS server with IP address 192.168.1.1 is deployed in a data center. A network engineer must configure a Cisco UCS Fabric Interconnect to use this DNS.
Which configuration should be applied?
options: ficl-mgmt-A# scope fabric-interconnect a / ficl-mgmt-A /fabric-interconnect # set name 192.168.1.1 ficl-mgmt-A /fabric-interconnect # scope system ficl-mgmt-A /system # commit-buffer
ficl-mgmt-A# scope system ficl-mgmt-A /system # create dns 192.168.1.1 ficl-mgmt-A /system* # commit-buffer
ficl-mgmt-A# scope fabric-interconnect a ficl-mgmt-A /fabric-interconnect # set name 192.168.1.1 ficl-mgmt-A /fabric-interconnect* # commit-buffer
ficl-mgmt-A# scope system ficl-mgmt-A /system # scope services ficl-mgmt-A /system/services # create dns 192.168.1.1 ficl-mgmt-A /system/services* # commit-buffer
theory: In the Cisco UCS Manager CLI, system-wide administrative services such as DNS, NTP, and the default time zone live under the 'system/services' scope, not directly under 'system' or under a fabric-interconnect scope (which configures per-FI identity, not shared services). To add a DNS server you must therefore descend scope system > scope services before issuing 'create dns <ip>' and committing the buffer. Options that try to set the DNS address as the fabric interconnect 'name' or skip the services sub-scope target the wrong object and will not configure name resolution for the cluster. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Initial Setup and UCS Manager)
